title: ergomap data
description: An article's reasoning as a graph: theses (starting claims and conclusions) and which theses each conclusion follows from, with an optional analysis.

id.description: Positive integer as in a numbered chain, or a short slug. Shown as [id] and used in the URL as #t<id>.

reasoningType.description: The rule by which the step gets from its premises to its conclusion. Defaults to deductive.

condition.description: What a non-deductive step relies on without saying so, rated by its reasoning type's criteria.

text.description: The condition as a sentence, e.g. "Nothing else explains the effect."

reason.description: Why it has this rating, in a few words.

pool.description: Premises of this step that are alternative evidence for the conclusion; they count as one premise.

versionThesis.description: A thesis of the reconstructed or optimized logic. Label, text, note and section default to the thesis with the same id in the version it's built from; from and pool are never inherited.

from.description: The theses this one follows from in this version. Empty or missing for a starting claim.

pool.description: Premises in from that are alternative evidence for the conclusion; they count as one premise.

steps.description: Instead of from, type, condition and pool: separate steps of different reasoning types for one conclusion.

verdict.description: For a starting claim: how well its backing matches what it says.

reason.description: Why the starting claim has its verdict, pointing to its backing in the article.

fixes.description: Ids of the issues whose fix added or changed this thesis.

flaw.description: Id of a flaw with no fix that breaks this step; its strength is 0.

target.description: inference: a conclusion and, optionally, the premises at fault; thesis: one thesis; pair: two theses; concept: a term from concepts; argument: the whole argument.

theses.description: The theses involved, ids from the original logic.

concept.description: For a concept target: the term, as in concepts.

quote.description: A short quote from the article that shows the issue.

senses.description: Usually one; a term the article uses in two senses lists both.

lang.description: BCP 47 language of the content, e.g. "en" or "pt-BR". Picks the UI strings.

sections.description: Optional grouping of theses, shown above the selected thesis.

theses.description: The original logic, in reading order. Prev/next and arrow keys follow this order.

label.description: Short node caption, two to four words. The viewer wraps it; "\n" forces a line break.

text.description: The claim as a complete standalone sentence.

from.description: Ids of the theses this one follows from. Empty or missing for a starting claim.

note.description: Context from the source: examples, quotes, references. Markdown links [text](https://…) become links.

start.description: Thesis selected when the page opens. Defaults to the first one.

strings.description: UI strings for a language without a built-in dictionary, or overrides. Keys are listed in locales/index.json.

analysis.description: Optional argument analysis. With it the page opens on a summary and adds an audit and the reconstructed and optimized logic; strength is computed by the viewer.

reconstructed.description: The original made explicit: every thesis with its verdict or its step, implicit premises added, bundled theses split, fixes applied.

optimized.description: The reconstructed logic reduced to the fewest starting claims that keep every final conclusion at the same strength. Ids only from the reconstructed logic.
